source_refs.note: Topic 2.6.3, printed pages 33-34: the d and f orbitals (Figure 2.7) and Quick Check 2.4.

blocks.text: In a given shell, ‘d’ orbitals have different shapes and orientations in space. The dxy, dxz, and dyz lie in the xy, xz, and yz planes, respectively. The lobes of the dx²−y² lie along the x and y axes. The dz² orbital has two lobes along the z-axis and a “doughnut” in the xy plane.
The shapes for the five d orbitals (ℓ = 2,) are shown in Figure 2.7.

blocks.alt: Five 3d orbitals on x, y and z axes, in the printed order: dz2 (two lobes along z and a ring in the xy plane), dx2-y2 (four lobes along the x and y axes), dxy (four lobes between the x and y axes), dyz (four lobes between the y and z axes) and dxz (four lobes between the x and z axes). Shaded and white lobes show opposite phases.
blocks.caption: Fig. 2.7: The shapes of the five 3d orbitals (original drawing after the textbook's Fig. 2.7).

blocks.text: An f subshell has seven orientations in space, i.e. there are seven f orbitals. However, the shapes of f orbitals are very complicated.
